facts.statement: Fossils of Zhyraornis were discovered in the Bissekty Formation near Dzharakuduk in the Kyzyl Kum desert of Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in Bissekty Formation deposits near Dzharakuduk in the Kyzyl Kum, Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: The only known fossils of Zhyraornis consist of partial pelvic bones known as synsacra.
facts.quote: Both are known only from partial pelvic bones (synsacra).

facts.statement: Zhyraornis lived during the late Cretaceous period, specifically the middle Turonian stage, approximately 92 million years ago.
facts.quote: Zhyraornis is a genus of prehistoric bird from the late Cretaceous period (middle Turonian, 92 mya).

facts.statement: Paleontologist Lev Nesov originally classified Zhyraornis in the family Zhyraornithidae and the suborder Zhyraornithi within the order Ichthyornithiformes.
facts.quote: Paleontologist Lev Nesov originally classified in a distinct family (Zhyraornithidae) and later suborder (Zhyraornithi) within the order Ichthyornithiformes.

facts.statement: In 1996, Kurochkin reclassified Zhyraornis as a member of the family Alexornithidae within the Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: Kurochkin (1996) considered it to belong to the Enantiornithes, specifically the family Alexornithidae.

facts.statement: In 2006, Kurochkin reclassified Zhyraornis as a primitive member of the Ornithuromorpha, the lineage leading to modern birds.
facts.quote: In 2006, Kurochkin re-classified it as a primitive member of the lineage leading to modern birds, the Ornithuromorpha.

facts.statement: The exact evolutionary relationships of Zhyraornis remain unresolved among scientists.
facts.quote: The relationships of this bird are unresolved.

facts.statement: The time range for Zhyraornis spans from the Cenomanian to the Turonian, between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Turonian (100.5 to 89.8 million years ago)
